newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PALMEIRO HOMER EVENS SERIES FOR ORIOLES AGAINST YANKS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PALMEIRO HOMER EVENS SERIES FOR ORIOLES AGAINST YANKS.

text.p: Rafael Palmeiro's two-run home run in the seventh inning put the Baltimore Orioles ahead to stay in a 5-3 win over the New York Yankees Thursday that evened their American League Championship Series at a game apiece.

After Wednesday night's bizarre and dramatic Yankee win that saw a protested Derek Jeter home run assisted by a 12-year-old fan and an 11th-inning Bernie Williams homer, the Orioles' victory built on two homers and good pitching was almost routine.
But it sent them home for the middle three games of the best-of-seven series with a welcome split in Yankee Stadium.

"I have a team of professionals who didn't let the loss in a tough defeat put them on an emotional roller coaster," said Baltimore manager Davey Johnson. "We came here, played tough and won the game."

Palmeiro smacked a 3-1 pitch from reliever Jeff Nelson 364 feet over the right-field fence with Roberto Alomar aboard to break a 2-2 tie. The runs marked this year's first post-season failure by the Yankee bullpen, which had four victories and yielded just one earned run in 23 and 2/3 innings.
Todd Zeile also had a two-run homer for the slugging Orioles.
"We don't bunt, we don't play hit and run, we hit the ball out of the ball park," said Johnson.
Baltimore starter David Wells got the win and Nelson the loss. Armando Benitez, who got Cecil Fielder and Tino Martinez to fly out in the ninth with two men aboard, got the save.
"I love Yankee Stadium," said Wells. "I have an autograph of Babe Ruth in 1903 on the sweet spot on a ball. I pitch good here and I love.
"We bounced back from a tough defeat and didn't let it bother us. This was a great win."
"We struggled at times all year as far as getting runs is concerned," said New York manager Joe Torre. "You have got to give David Wells credit. We had chances, but they pitched better than us."
The Yanks broke out on top in the first inning.

Williams hit an RBI line single to right after Jeter and Tim Raines pushed nearly identical line singles to right centre. A double play on a Fielder grounder gave the Yankees their second run and it was 2-0.
Yankee starter David Cone had loaded the bases with three walks in the first but got out of the jam when Cal Ripken, after fouling off a couple with a 3-2 count, flied out to centre field.

But in the third, Cone's shaky control hurt him when he yielded a leadoff walk to Brady Anderson -- after getting ahead 0-2 -- and Zeile homered into the left-field stands on a 3-1 count. That tied the game at 2-2.
Wells wiggled out of trouble in the fifth. Joe Girardi hit a leadoff triple but was stranded when Jeter struck out, Raines walked, Williams struck out and Fielder grounded out.
"The key to the game was when we got the triple and couldn't score," said Torre.

But Cone had a greater escape in the bottom of the inning. Ripken got a one-out single, a soft flare just about Tino Martinez's glove at first. One out later B.J. Surhoff also singled and then Chris Hoiles walked, loading the bases.
Torre went to the mound and, after a long conference, left Cone in to face the dangerous Anderson, who then flied out to left to strand three runners.
But that was Cone's last batter. He had thrown 133 pitches, his highest of the season in 11 starts before and after surgery for an aneurysm in his shoulder.
Nelson came on in the seventh and yielded the Palmeiro homer scoring Alomar, who had doubled.
"Jeff (Nelson) got the ball up and out over the plate," said Palmeiro. "I think he was trying to walk me and didn't put it where he wanted to."
The Yanks got one run back in the bottom of the seventh on Fielder's RBI single, bringing home Girardi.

But in the eighth, the Orioles went up 5-3 when Anderson and Zeile singled with one out and Alomar brought in the run on a foul-pop sacrifice fly to right. The Baltimore bullpen made the score stand up.
Game 3 is in Baltimore Friday.
